title: Ship endpoint is an admin-only action with no role or ownership check
owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry
rationale: Root cause: the /api/orders/ship route (src/Ordering.API/Apis/OrdersApi.cs:12) inherits only the group-level RequireAuthorization() from Program.cs:22, which checks "is authenticated" and nothing else. ShipOrderCommandHandler.Handle (ShipOrderCommandHandler.cs:19) is a domain handler with no caller context, so the check belongs at the route. The change adds a named authorization policy "OrderAdministrator" (Extensions.cs, right after AddDefaultAuthentication) and attaches it to the ship route only. Endpoint-level policies combine with the group-level one (both must pass), so the caller must be authenticated and hold the admin role. The policy passes if the principal is in role "admin" (ClaimTypes.Role) or has a raw "role"="admin" claim. I check both because the JWT claim-type mapping may or may not turn "role" into ClaimTypes.Role. Deployer must configure: the Identity provider (src/Identity.API) must issue a "role" claim with value "admin" in the access token for administrator accounts. It does not issue one today, so until that is configured every caller gets 403 on /ship, which fails closed. I did not add any role system to Identity.API. Tests: the ship functional test middleware can now add a role claim from an "x-test-role" request header, and the two existing ship tests send "admin" so they keep their current expectations. The auth fixture has no role by default.
variants_checked: OrdersApi.cs:CancelOrderAsync (/cancel). Same missing-role pattern, but cancelling is a legitimate customer action. It is a separate ownership/BOLA concern, not this finding, so left alone. OrdersApi.cs:CreateOrderDraftAsync, CreateOrderAsync, GetOrderAsync and GetOrdersByUserAsync are not admin actions, so no change. ShipOrderCommand is dispatched only from ShipOrderAsync (grep in src/Ordering.API). No other routes or consumers invoke it, and the integration-event path does not. grep for AddPolicy/RequireRole across src and tests found no existing policy, so nothing to reuse.
bypass_considered: Attacker with a normal user token calls PUT /api/orders/ship directly. The route policy now returns 403. Attacker supplies a self-asserted "role" claim in the request body or headers: it is not read, since claims come only from the validated JWT. Attacker sends the x-test-role header: only the test middleware reads it, and it is not registered in production. Attacker reaches the ship command another way (a different route or message): grep found none. A residual item: the admin role must be issued only by the trusted identity provider, which is a deployment concern. If JWT validation is disabled (no Identity config section), authentication fails closed anyway.
test_note: Added ShipByNonAdminIsForbidden to tests/Ordering.FunctionalTests/OrderingApiTests.cs. It expects 403 for an authenticated non-admin PUT to api/orders/ship, and before the fix it returned 500 because the handler ran. It was not run (read-only, no build). The two existing Ship tests are adjusted to send an admin role header via AutoAuthorizeMiddleware.cs. Line numbers in hunks are approximate, from the file contents as read.
review_reason: The `.RequireAuthorization("OrderAdministrator")` hunk at `OrdersApi.cs:12` closes the missing role check in front of `ShipOrderCommandHandler.Handle` (line 19), the only caller path. The `Extensions.cs` policy hunk and the test hunks are in scope and add no new input parsing or weakened validation. The `role=admin` claim is not issued anywhere in the repo, so the endpoint stays locked until a deployer provisions it. That is fail-closed, and the diff should document it.
